entities.summary: John William King was an American lawyer, jurist, and Democratic politician from Manchester, New Hampshire. He received his undergraduate degree from Harvard College and his law degree from Columbia Law School in 1943. He practiced law in Manchester and served in the New Hampshire House of Representatives. In 1962 he was elected governor of New Hampshire, becoming only the third Democratic governor of New Hampshire in 88 years, and the first since Fred Herbert Brown lost the 1924 election. After his three terms as the 71st governor of New Hampshire, he served on the New Hampshire Supreme Court from 1979, and as its Chief Justice from 1981 until 1986.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: John W. King's election as governor of New Hampshire in 1962 marked a significant shift for the state's Democratic Party, which had not held the office since 1924. His three-term tenure and subsequent service on the New Hampshire Supreme Court demonstrate his lasting impact on the state's politics.
